title: Endurance
summary:
Endurance training is presented as a necessity in pregnancy. Pregnancy changes the cardiovascular, respiratory and other systems, and oxygen uptake capacity decreases toward the third trimester, so aerobic training helps optimize cardiovascular function and reduce the burden on the body. Benefits include weight control, better cardiorespiratory capacity, lower gestational diabetes risk, better blood pressure, mood and labor preparation.

The chapter describes continuous low-to-moderate aerobic exercise, adapted intervals, combined circuits, aquatic exercise and adapted HIIT for active women. It gives intensity targets of 40-60% of heart rate reserve and RPE 12-14, three sample programs for sedentary, active and athlete women, trimester adjustments, and advice to progress gradually with professional supervision.
points: Intensity should stay at 40-60% of heart rate reserve and RPE 12-14, adjusted each trimester.
Continuous aerobic exercise runs 20-60 min at a steady pace (walking, cycling, swimming, elliptical, water aerobics), using the talk test.
Intervals for previously active women can be 1 min of effort followed by 2 min of recovery, limited to 80% of usual perceived exertion.
Combined aerobic and strength circuits are described as the most beneficial modality for maternal health.
Water exercise gives a lower maternal heart rate for the same oxygen consumption than land-based activity.
Adapted HIIT suits active women or athletes, using 30-40 s of work and 15-20 s of rest, for example two blocks of 8 sets of 30 s work and 20 s rest.
The sedentary program is 3 sessions per week, progressing from 20 to 30-35 min over 6-8 weeks at 30-50% of heart rate reserve and RPE 10-13, reaching at least 150 min per week.

The active program is 4-5 sessions per week of 30 progressing to 40-45 min at RPE 12-14, with 150-180 min per week; the athlete program is 5-6 sessions of 40 progressing to 55-60 min, with 200-250 min per week.
Progress by increasing duration, then frequency, and finally intensity, and split sessions (for example two 15-min sets) if fatigued.
takeaways: Use the talk test and RPE 12-14 to set effort.
Pick low-impact options such as walking, cycling, elliptical or swimming, especially in later trimesters.
Progress step by step with the weekly session-length plan for your profile.
Split a 30-min session into two 15-min blocks when tired.
Combine aerobic work with moderate strength.
Stay hydrated, avoid heat, and adjust each trimester with your professional team.
cautions: Avoid lying on your back from the second trimester onward because of inferior vena cava compression.
Stop and watch for warning signs such as dizziness, bleeding, contractions, excessive shortness of breath or abdominal pain.
Avoid maximal efforts, high-impact exercise, jumping and rapid changes of direction; avoid prolonged anaerobic exercise, which can cause hyperthermia and dehydration.
